To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

microinjection of the organophosphate mevinphos into the rostral ventral lateral medulla (RVIM) depresses mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activities and induces cardiovascular toxicity, which can be prevented by comicroinjection with atropine into the RVIM.

mevinphos, a cholinester-ase inhibitor, induces a progressive depression in mitochondrial respiratory enzyme activities in the rostral ventro-lateral medulla, a brainstem site where sympathetic vas-omotor tone originates, which is associated with the development of cardiovascular toxicity.

microinjection of Mev (10 nmoles) into the rostral ventro-lateral medulla (a medullary site that is the origin for sympathetic vasomotor control) of the rat elicited a progressive hypotension accompanied by a selective and progressive depression of the activity of NADD cytochrome c-reductase (Complexes I and III), cytochrome c-oxidase (Complex IV) in the respiratory chain of the mitochondria in the RVLM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanisms by which Mev induces cardiovascular intoxication.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that lead to cardiovascular toxicity induced by organophosphates.
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of Mev in the RVLM and the role of mitochondrial dysfunction in the cardiovascular consequences of Mev intoxication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present findings suggest that the cardiovascular consequences of Mev intoxication are mediated via muscarinic receptor activation and that the resultant dysfunction of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes in the RVLM may be the basis for the development of cardiovascular toxicity associated with Mev and possibly other cholinesterase-inhibiting organophosphate poiso
the depression of the activity of respiratory chain enzymes in the RVLM may be a critical factor in the pathogenesis of organophosphate-induced cholinergic toxicity.

the present findings provide evidence that the cholinergic mechanism in the RVLM may be involved in the pathogenesis of cardiovascular toxicity associated with acute intoxication by organophosphate poison such as Mev.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cholinergic muscarinic system plays a critical role in the bioenergetics of the RVLM and that the dysfunction of this system by Mev is a critical factor that underlies the cardiovascular toxicity of this organophosphate poison in the rat.
the RVLM is a site where mevinphos acts to elicit its cardiovascular toxicity.
the RVLM is a site of action for the organophosphate pesticide mevinphos.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cardiovascular effects of organophosphate poisson such as mevinphos are mediated through a cholinergic mechanism at the rostral medulla, which involves a selective depression of respiratory enzyme Complex I and IV in mitochondria.
the cardiovascular effects of Mev are mediated by the muscarinic receptor in the rostral ventral lateral medulla.

the organophosphate pesticide mevinphos acts to depress the activity of mitochondrial enzymes in the rostral ventral lateral medulla (RVML), a medullar site where sympathetic vasodilatory tone originates and where mevinphos elicits cardiovascular intoxication.
